version.changelog: 0.3.3 risk hardening: security headers + restricted CORS on dashboard, explicit hook capabilities in manifest, expanded Known Risks table in docs. Legitimate local monitoring tool for OpenClaw LLM API resilience. (JSON fixed)

llm.summary: This skill is a clearly disclosed companion interface for a local resilience plugin, with no artifact evidence of deception or data theft.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is monitoring API errors, reports, retry strategies, and a dashboard; the listed tools and dashboard UI align with that purpose, including strategy mutation controls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Natural-language examples include state-changing strategy updates and dashboard opening, but they are presented as explicit examples rather than hidden triggers; users should still confirm mutating requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill requires installing a separate @leiJack-lo/resilience plugin with --dangerously-force-unsafe-install, and the documentation discloses why: local server, browser opening, hooks, and local file writes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local HTTP dashboard access, model-call hooks, and ~/.openclaw/plugins/resilience storage are proportionate to error monitoring and retry management, but they are higher-impact than a documentation-only skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistence is disclosed as local JSON/JSONL stats, strategies, active retries, and tasks under the resilience plugin directory; no unrelated persistence or privilege escalation appears in the skill artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want the companion plugin to monitor OpenClaw model-call errors, run a local dashboard, and modify retry strategy files. Treat strategy changes as operational changes: confirm them intentionally, keep the dashboard bound to localhost, and review the plugin package itself before using the forced unsafe install flag.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] expected: The dashboard is expected to send write requests for retry strategy management. The client disables most edits when the backend reports non-editable, but the reset action relies on server enforcement, so backend scoping remains important.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation phrases map to the skill's advertised monitoring and retry-management functions. They are somewhat broad for mutating strategy changes, but the behavior is disclosed and purpose-aligned.
